correctness.rationale: Periodic integration by parts gives X=int cos(nt)dnu and Y=int cos(2nt)dnu=2int u^2 dnu for the zero-mass signed derivative nu=df. Equal Jordan masses m<=1/2 and adding common mass reduce the image to X=(a-b)/2, Y=r-s where a,b are probability first moments on [-1,1] and r in [a^2,1],s in [b^2,1]. For fixed X, min |b|=max(0,2|X|-1), so the exact upper cap is 1-b^2, and reflection gives lower cap; convexity fills every vertical section and integration gives 10/3. The homogeneous gauge has branches |Y| for |Y|>=2|X| and 4|X|^2/(4|X|-|Y|) otherwise. Equality r=1 and s=b^2 forces the asserted +/- endpoint and point masses, with lifts to 2 or 3 step-function jumps; no unique original-circle location is implied for n>1. This is an analytic all-n argument; CHECK.py contains only rational consistency points.
